## fence-check

The worker write fence's decision for one path as a card's lane would get it, and why. Reads only.

It checks its own options (the usage above lists them).

## init

cockpit init [DIR]: a first pack for a workspace. It prints what it detected and the files it would write, and writes nothing without --write. It never replaces a file, and it never guesses what production is: that takes --production-host REGEX (repeatable) or --no-production. The binding file is written last, once the pack loads.

Example:

```
cockpit init --no-production
cockpit init ~/work/shop --production-host 'app\.example\.test' --write
```

Options: `--accept-gates`, `--json`, `--no-bind`, `--no-production`, `--no-starter`, `--pack`, `--production-host`, `--project`, `--rebind`, `--slots`, `--staging-origin`, `--tracker`, `--tracker-url`, `--write`, `--yes`.

## pack

cockpit pack check [--all] | effective [--json] [--sources] | explain <key> [--json] | pin [--all] [--json]: the bound pack, checked (with --all: every problem it has, not only the first); every setting with the value in force (and where it came from); one key with its meaning; the lines that write out each value the pack takes from a default that will change (with --all, from any default).

Example:

```
cockpit pack check [--all]
cockpit pack effective [--json] [--sources]
cockpit pack explain forge.bump_batch [--json]
cockpit pack pin [--all] [--json]
```

Options: `--all`, `--json`, `--sources`.

## describe

cockpit describe --json: this kernel's verbs, intent types, kickoff modes, card kinds and marks, as data. It reads no workspace and no pack.

Example:

```
cockpit describe --json
```

Options: `--json`.

## demo

cockpit demo gate [--yes] [--keep]: the outbox gate shown working in a sandbox under the temp folder, with no Hermes, no forge account and no tracker. It needs no bound workspace and touches none. --yes does not wait for Enter before the publish; --keep leaves the sandbox to look at.

Example:

```
cockpit demo gate [--yes] [--keep]
```

Options: `--keep`, `--yes`.

Example:


Options: `--rerender`, `--seat`.

## update

cockpit update check | status | apply [--to <commit>] [--no-restart] | rollback [--to <commit>] [--no-restart] | rehome <url> [--branch <name>] [--dry-run] | rehome --undo: the plugin against its own repository.

Example:

```
cockpit update check
cockpit update apply [--to <commit>] [--no-restart]
cockpit update rollback [--to <commit>] [--no-restart]
cockpit update rehome https://example.test/team/cockpit.git [--branch main] [--dry-run]
cockpit update rehome --undo
```

Options: `--branch`, `--dry-run`, `--no-restart`, `--to`, `--undo`.

## apply

Example:

```
cockpit apply
```

It takes no argument.

## doctor

cockpit doctor [--strict] [--json] [--online]: the errors, then the warnings, each with the line that resolves it. Only an error fails it; --strict makes a warning fail too, and no flag makes an error pass. --online adds the probes that need the network. A note is printed after the verdict and never changes it.

Example:

```
cockpit doctor [--strict] [--json] [--online]
```

Options: `--json`, `--online`, `--strict`.

## outbox

Usage:

```
cockpit outbox new <ticket> <type> --card <id> --summary <text> [payload flags]
amend <id> [--summary <text>] [--top-level] [payload flags]
list [<ticket>]
show <id>
endorse <id> <risk> [notes]
hold <id> --reason <text> [--waits lane] [--rework <text> [--chain]] [--ask <question> --option <answer>...]
return <id> --instruction <text> [--assignee <lane>] [--evidence <path>]... [--no-chain]
drop <id> [--note <text>]
verify <id>
reprobe <id>
ack <id>
digest
reconcile [<ticket>]
sweep
rework <ticket> --instruction <text> [--repo <repo>] [--evidence <path>]...
chain <ticket> <after-card> --instruction <text> [--repo <repo>]
relink <id> --waits-for <id>
```

Example:

```
cockpit outbox new TASK-100 push-branch --card t_1 --summary 'push the export' --repo api --branch work/TASK-100
```

It checks its own options (the usage above lists them).

## guard

An editor agent's pre-tool hook: its JSON on stdin. Outside the lanes, a slot, vault, or publishing command, a vault or slot path, or a lane's account is refused (exit 2, the reason on stderr and in the block JSON both common editor hook formats read).

Example:

```
cockpit guard < hook-input.json
```

## publish

cockpit publish --id <intent> [--dry-run] [--approve] | --all: every endorsed intent in digest order, stopping at the first refusal.

Example:

```
cockpit publish --id TASK-100/001-push-branch --dry-run
```

Options: `--all`, `--approve`, `--dry-run`, `--id`.

## helper

The pack's helpers (helpers.yaml): start, stop and see the dev stack and local services.

Usage:

```
cockpit helper list
status [--group G] [--json]
options NAME
run NAME VERB [--choice C] [--background]
```

Example:

```
cockpit helper run web start
```

Options: `--background`, `--choice`, `--group`, `--json`, `--run-id`.

## reply

cockpit reply "<publish all | publish 1-3,5 | hold 4: why | drop 5 | open 2>": the answer to the last digest.

Example:

```
cockpit reply 'publish 1-3'
```

## ci

cockpit ci flaky|real <ticket> <sha> [--run-id N] [--repo R]: the analyst's verdict on a failed CI run.

Example:

```
cockpit ci flaky TASK-100 <sha> --run-id 42
```

It checks its own options (the usage above lists them).

## test

cockpit test plan <ticket> <file>: post the test plan and wait for go. test fail <ticket> <row> "<note>": the one recording of a failed row. test run-dir <ticket>: the folder the next run writes to.

Example:

```
cockpit test plan TASK-100 plan.md
test fail TASK-100 3 'what broke'
test run-dir TASK-100
```

It checks its own options (the usage above lists them).

## flow

cockpit flow decompose <ticket> <file>: intake's breakdown after go becomes the linked cards. flow reopen <ticket> "<what changed>": a lane reopens its own ticket; intake proposes again.

Example:

```
cockpit flow decompose TASK-100 breakdown.json
flow reopen TASK-100 'what changed'
```

It checks its own options (the usage above lists them).

## pace

`cockpit pace --json`: the plan pace for the supervisor (cockpitlib.pace). Exits 0 with a wrong flag value or an unreadable plan in `error`; an unknown flag is refused before it runs (exit 2), as for every command. Without --json the same answer as one line per window.

Example:

```
cockpit pace --json [--days 0,1,2,3,4] [--start HH:MM] [--end HH:MM] [--peak] [--fresh]
```

Options: `--days`, `--end`, `--fresh`, `--json`, `--peak`, `--start`.

## record

cockpit record start|stop|status: one reproduction video of a failed scenario on a test kickoff card (cockpitlib.record). Every value is a flag; a wrong shape prints the usage and does not run (exit 2); a refusal or a video that does not play exits 1 with the reason; success prints JSON.

Example:

```
cockpit record start --session tester-1-TASK-100 --out hermes/qa/TASK-100/run-1/evidence/videos/s3-save-button-repro.mp4 --record-id 'order 4711' --on-screen 'the saved order, form open' [--max-seconds 180] [--url-contains /orders]
record stop --session tester-1-TASK-100
record status
```

It checks its own options (the usage above lists them).
